brief: Goldman's recap of day three of its Communacopia and Technology conference, drawing on its research, European TMT and sales and trading desks. The through-line is that AI demand is broadening while supply stays tight, so the binding constraint has moved downstream from chips to power, land and datacenter capacity, and Goldman's own view is that downstream constraints matter more at the margin. Nvidia reiterated $3-4tn of AI infrastructure spending by 2030, reaffirmed roughly 70% CY27 growth, argued lower inference costs expand adoption, and rejected the circular financing framing of its guarantees. That tightness feeds the supply chain: 8-10 new fabs in 2027 support wafer fab equipment acceleration, Lam calls the industry sold out with DRAM leading 2027 spend, Seagate sees pricing and the HAMR transition carrying earnings through FY27. The note then reports, without resolving, the central debate. Bottom-up indicators are constructive, but investors remain hesitant to re-commit to the AI infrastructure trade, customers are shifting from token maxing to ROI-led token optimising, and proof is still needed that capex converts into durable revenue, margins and cash flow. Cybersecurity, agent-led software and single-company updates fill out the day.
